name: Skillsoft Corp.

profile.description: Skillsoft provides corporate learning content and platforms through Talent Development Solutions ($404M) and Global Knowledge ($109M, down 13%). FY2026 revenue fell 3.4% to $513M with adjusted EBITDA of $110M (21% margin) and free cash flow of only $6M versus $12M, and the $51M market cap reflects heavy leverage.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track record 1: AI skills platform and coaching rollout under new CEO Jeff Tarr [1][2]. AI 1: employees describe an AI-first culture but no quantified AI revenue or savings found [2]. Share 1: meaningful but not leading player in corporate learning; R&D 1: near industry average; no named pipeline (0).

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission floor 2: clear learning-for-workforce mission, not distinctive [1]. Glassdoor shows only 40% recommend, 2.8/5 culture and values, so retention scores 0 [2]; no insider buying or community evidence found.

infrastructure.label: WEAK
infrastructure.analysis: Liquidity floor triggered: 72,892 avg daily shares x $5.64 = about $411K, below $1M, so Infrastructure = 0. D/E and ROE unavailable.

ai_resilience.label: HIGH RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: Generative AI directly commoditizes standardized skills content and course libraries, Skillsoft's core revenue, while global knowledge instructor-led training is declining 13% [1]. Enterprise purchasing is cautious and the company has no clear moat against AI tutors; no AI revenue is quantified.

infinite_game.summary: Revenue declining, morale low and leadership turnover; operating for survival under leverage rather than a long-term cause.

just_cause.analysis: Purpose to democratize learning exists but reads as marketing and has not shaped consistent strategy through repeated leadership changes [1].

trusting_teams.analysis: Glassdoor: 40% recommend, 2.8/5 culture, morale described as at an all-time low under new CEO, with frequent executive churn [2].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Evolved from content library to AI skills platform; incremental adaptation [1].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Investing in AI-first product during revenue decline is one costly bet, but largely forced by market pressure [1][2].

investment_thesis: Skillsoft holds $404M of Talent Development revenue (flat) and 21% adjusted EBITDA margins, with an AI-first pivot that could stabilize content demand [1]. A 1.2x forward P/E signals deep-value optionality if free cash flow improves.
thesis_continued: FY2026 revenue fell 3.4% to $513M, Global Knowledge fell 13%, free cash flow halved to $6M and GAAP margin is -32%, with a $51M market cap against a leveraged balance sheet [1]. GenAI directly substitutes standardized training content, employee sentiment is poor (2.8/5 culture), and daily dollar volume of about $411K fails the liquidity floor [2].
key_catalysts: Traction for the AI Skills platform stabilizing Talent Development revenue
Return to growth with enterprise purchasing recovery
key_risks: GenAI tutors and free content commoditize the core library
sources: Skillsoft Q4 and FY2026 Results, investor.skillsoft.com, 2026
Skillsoft Glassdoor reviews and leadership, Glassdoor, 2026
